summary: Two changed Scaladoc blocks overstate behavior that the implementation does not guarantee.

items.issue: The class is public and extensible, so the code does not enforce that each value type has a single manifest instance. Clients can define multiple `AnyValManifest[Int]` instances; they compare unequal by reference, despite describing the same value type.
items.suggestion: Limit the singleton claim to the canonical manifests supplied by `Manifest`/`ManifestFactory`, or state directly that equality for `AnyValManifest` instances is by reference identity.

items.issue: The description says the final rendered part is the type arguments, but `argString` renders the bracketed component type when `typeArguments` is empty and `runtimeClass` is an array class. For example, a manifest made from an array class with no explicit arguments includes that component type.
items.suggestion: Describe the final part as `argString`, explaining that it is explicit type arguments when present, otherwise the bracketed component type for array runtime classes.
